design.objective: Allow configuration administrators to bind each release-approval scenario to a published workflow per project, with backend resolution, immutable running-version semantics, auditability and workflow lifecycle protection.
users: Configuration administrators bind five release scenarios for the current project.
Project developers submit release applications without selecting or typing workflow identifiers.
Workflow administrators maintain definitions while the platform protects referenced and historical definitions.
Auditors inspect binding changes and immutable workflow history.

requirements.statement: Configuration management must expose five fixed approval scenarios whose published-workflow bindings are isolated by tenant and project.
acceptance: project switching loads the corresponding bindings
each project and scene has at most one binding
the user selects a published workflow instead of typing a code
requirements.source: User confirmed a separate configuration-management page and project-specific bindings on 2026-08-17.
counterexample: workflow graph is edited from the binding page

requirements.statement: Projects may save partial bindings, while submission must fail atomically only when its resolved scenario is unbound or references a non-published definition.
acceptance: failed submission creates no round, instance or status transition
requirements.source: User approved fixed scenes with partial configuration and hit-time blocking.
counterexample: missing emergency binding blocks regular submissions
a failed start leaves a STARTING round

requirements.statement: The release backend must resolve the project-scene binding by workflow definition ID and freeze the actual definition version and instance on each submitted round.
acceptance: new submissions use the binding committed at submission time
existing submissions continue on their original definition version after rebinding
the frontend cannot choose a workflow in the application payload
requirements.source: User approved that binding changes affect only future applications.

requirements.statement: Binding changes must require a reason, preserve before and after values with operator and time, enforce tenant/project authorization and reject stale writes.
acceptance: create, update and unbind history is queryable
cross-project and cross-tenant access is denied
requirements.source: User approved traceable binding lifecycle behavior.
counterexample: only the final value is retained
last writer silently overwrites a concurrent update

requirements.statement: Only never-published definitions with no instances and no active business binding may be deleted; an actively bound definition may not be archived.
acceptance: a pure draft can be soft-deleted
a formerly published draft cannot be deleted
requirements.source: User confirmed workflow lifecycle and reference-protection rules.
counterexample: unpublish then delete bypasses history protection
archiving a bound definition breaks future release submissions

invariants: running instances remain bound to their original definition and version
all definitions, bindings and queries are tenant scoped
project context remains a stable interface while its current source is mocked
unrelated rokey worktree changes remain untouched
constraints: existing WorkflowBusinessGateway and release lifecycle consumer remain the integration boundary
non_goals: workflow graph editing from configuration management
manual workflow choice on a release application
automatic creation of approval graphs or assignees
changes to release scenario classification rules
